fixes.e: A user delegation SAS is signed with a user delegation key obtained through Microsoft Entra ID, making it more secure than key-signed tokens. Account SAS and service SAS are signed with the storage account key, and ad hoc only describes a SAS whose start, expiry, and permissions are set in the URI rather than a stored access policy - any SAS type, including user delegation, can be ad hoc.
fixes._why: The explanation asserts that ad hoc SAS tokens are all signed with the storage account key, which is false - a user delegation SAS is always an ad hoc SAS and is signed with Microsoft Entra credentials, not the account key. [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview]

fixes.e: Choosing the Container publish option (formerly labeled Docker Container) lets App Service pull and run a container image. The Code option deploys application source directly, and a function app is a separate resource type.
fixes._why: The keyed option uses the superseded portal label "Docker Container"; since the 2024 sidecar update the App Service create flow's Publish option is named "Container". [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/quickstart-custom-container]

fixes.x: An administrator wants to record IP traffic flowing through a virtual network to a storage account for later analysis. Which Network Watcher capability provides this?
fixes.e: Virtual network flow logs capture ingress and egress IP traffic metadata to a storage account for later analysis and traffic analytics, and they replace the retiring NSG flow logs feature, which no longer allows new flow logs to be created. Effective security rules only display the aggregated rule set, not live traffic.
fixes._why: The item teaches NSG flow logs as the current way to start recording IP traffic to a storage account, but NSG flow logs are retiring (September 30, 2027) and new NSG flow logs can no longer be created; Microsoft's replacement is virtual network flow logs. [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/nsg-flow-logs-overview]

fixes.x: Which Azure VM backup policy type supports multiple backups per day and newer disk offerings such as Ultra Disk and Premium SSD v2?
fixes.e: The Enhanced backup policy supports hourly backups, as frequently as every four hours, and covers newer offerings such as Ultra Disk and Premium SSD v2. The Standard policy allows only one scheduled backup per day and does not protect those newer disk types; Trusted Launch VMs can now be backed up with either policy type.
fixes._why: The stem asserts the Enhanced policy is 'required to protect a Trusted Launch VM' and the explanation says the Standard policy 'does not cover Trusted Launch machines', but Azure Backup now supports Trusted Launch VM backup with the Standard policy (GA). [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-vms-enhanced-policy]
